name: much or many
rule: 'Many' and 'few' go with things you can count: many chairs, few cars.
'Much' and 'little' go with things you cannot count: much rice, little time.

wrong.text: There were too much people in the lift.

right.text: There were too many people in the lift.

spot: Can you put a number in front of the thing (three people)? Then it is 'many'.
deeper: 'Fewer' for counted things, 'less' for the rest: fewer cars, less noise.
'A number of' goes with counted things; 'an amount of' with the rest.
Money, water, time and advice cannot be counted this way: much advice.

extra.text: Grandma did not need much reasons to bake a cake on a Sunday.
extra.note: Reasons can be counted, so it is 'many'.

extra.text: We did not have many time left, so we ran to the bus stop.
extra.note: Time is not counted this way, so it is 'much'.

extra.text: The new shop does not get much visitors on weekday mornings.
extra.note: Visitors can be counted, so it is 'many'.

extra.text: After the storm, there was too many water on the court to play.
extra.note: Water is not counted one by one, so it is 'much'.
